name: South Carolina

law.statute: South Carolina Code s. 44-1-143 (Home-based Food Production)

gate.mechanism: Home-based food production operation meeting s. 44-1-143 is not a retail food establishment and needs no retail food permit from SCDA when producing non-potentially hazardous foods in a residential kitchen under the statute.
gate.fee_notes: No retail food permit fee under the home-based food production exemption. Optional SCDA home-based food ID number available if operator does not want a home address on the label.

channels.render_reason: s. 44-1-143 allows direct sales including online/mail and sales to retail stores within South Carolina
channels.notes: May sell directly to a person (including online and by mail order) or to retail stores, including grocery stores, within South Carolina. Retail stores must post signage that home-based foods are not subject to commercial food regulations. Operations with net earnings under $1,500 annually that would otherwise meet the definition are exempt from the labeling provisions of the section (not a general sales cap).

required_elements: Name and address of the home-based food production operation, or SCDA-issued identification number in place of address
Ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight
Conspicuous all-caps mandated disclaimer with clear contrast
Compliance with applicable federal labeling laws
labelling.mandated_disclaimer_text: PROCESSED AND PREPARED BY A HOME-BASED FOOD PRODUCTION OPERATION THAT IS NOT SUBJECT TO SOUTH CAROLINA'S FOOD SAFETY REGULATIONS.
labelling.allergen_rule: Federal labeling laws and regulations apply to packaged items

premises.inspection_frequency_basis: Not a retail food establishment under Reg. 61-25 when statute met

unique.quirk_paragraph:
South Carolina is unusually open on channels for a home-kitchen statute. Compliant home-based producers may sell direct to consumers (including online and mail order) and into retail stores inside the state, without a retail food permit.

There is no general sales-dollar ceiling on the exemption. The $1,500 net-earnings figure in the statute is a labeling carve-out for very small operations, not a statewide sales cap.

The label disclaimer is locked in all capital letters by statute and must contrast with the label background.
unique.common_mistake: Treating the $1,500 net-earnings figure as a hard sales limit, or using home-based food as a restaurant ingredient without an SCDA variance.
unique.what_does_not_apply: Potentially hazardous foods and out-of-state sales sit outside this home-based food production path.

information_gain: No retail food permit when s. 44-1-143 is met
Direct plus retail-store sales allowed in South Carolina; online/mail allowed
No general sales cap; $1,500 net is a labeling exemption only
All-caps statutory disclaimer required on packages
Retail food oversight moved to SCDA
